title: Probing Spatial and Temporal Hierarchies in Quantum Materials: Advances in High-Throughput Femtosecond Electron Microscopy
content: The development of a next-generation ultrafast electron microscope (UEM) platform at Michigan State University seeks to expand the frontiers of dynamical imaging of collective excitations by integrating high-brightness, high-throughput beam delivery with femtosecond temporal precision and multimodal capabilities. This RF-enabled UEM system moves beyond conventional ultrafast TEMs by incorporating optically controlled beam phase-space manipulation, enabling dynamic tuning of momentum, temporal, and spectral resolutions. A key innovation is the system’s ability to synchronize RF-based phase-space optics, facilitating high-intensity coherent beam formation while also breaking the temporal resolution barrier to achieve sub-100 fs precision. These technical advances allow us to challenge the conventional trade-off between brightness and throughput, enabling dynamical imaging across spatial and temporal scales with enhanced differential sensitivity [1].
